# Error-Handling Checklist: Feedback Sweep, slice 1 of 2 — the checkpoint

**Purpose**: Requirements-quality gate on the sweep's failure paths. The sweep
reads a live pull request, edits planning artifacts, commits, pushes, and writes
back to a reviewer, so every step has a way to fail partway. This checklist
tests whether the requirements say what happens on each of those paths, and in
particular whether "nothing to act on" and "could not read" are held apart
everywhere they meet.
**Created**: 2026-08-20
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

**Focus areas**: one behavior and one report shape per corroboration status; a
read that fails after the sweep began; a write that fails between the amendment
commit and its push; a reply that lands on one surface and fails on the other;
consensus outcomes that are not an answer. **Depth**: release gate.
**Audience**: reviewer (PR).

## Corroboration Status — One Behavior, One Report Shape

- [ ] CHK001 Are all six corroboration statuses assigned exactly one behavior each, with the mapping stated as exhaustive rather than by example? [Completeness, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the proceeding set held to exactly one status, so no second status can be read as proceeding? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the could-not-observe report required to name which of its four causes occurred, rather than reporting a generic failure? [Measurability, Spec §FR-019b]
- [ ] CHK004 Is the `no_record` / `skipped` distinction stated as a requirement — gate does not apply versus gate applies and observation failed — rather than left to a reader? [Clarity, Spec §FR-019a]
- [ ] CHK005 Is the could-not-observe report required to read differently from the three discrepancy stops? [Consistency, Spec §FR-019b]
- [x] CHK006 Is a resume path specified for each stopping status individually, rather than only for the two that carry one today? [Resolved, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK007 Is a corroboration value outside the closed six specified as a malformed observation with its own behavior, rather than falling through to a default? [Resolved, Spec §FR-019]
- [x] CHK008 Is the sweep's read-only relationship to the Draft PR row stated, so no stop path is allowed to rewrite the record it just failed to corroborate? [Resolved, Spec §FR-019]

## Mid-Sweep Read Failure — the Partial Observation

- [x] CHK009 Are requirements defined for a read that fails after the corroboration gate already returned `match`, given that the gate's statuses are observed before the reads begin? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [x] CHK010 Is the case where one comment surface reads cleanly and the other fails specified, rather than only the whole-pull-request-unreadable case? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [x] CHK011 Are requirements defined for pagination that fails partway through a multi-page read, where earlier pages are in hand and later pages are not? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [x] CHK012 Is an all-or-nothing observation invariant stated, so a partial candidate set can never reach classification? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [x] CHK013 Is it specified whether a partially observed run writes log rows, posts replies, or takes a bookkeeping commit before it stops? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [x] CHK014 Is the report shape for a mid-sweep read failure named, rather than the failure being an unreported halt? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [x] CHK015 Is a mid-sweep read failure required to be distinguishable in the report from the pre-read could-not-observe stop, given that the two have the same cause vocabulary but different amounts of work already done? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [x] CHK016 Can the claim that every trusted unrecorded comment carries a disposition be objectively verified when the observation itself may be incomplete? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]

## Write-Path Failure — Commit, Push, and the Recoverable State

- [x] CHK017 Are requirements defined for an amendment that commits locally but whose push fails, as distinct from the documented case of an amendment pushed without its bookkeeping commit? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012e]
- [x] CHK018 Is it specified what a re-run does when a local commit carries an amendment the remote has never seen, so the edit is present in the working tree but absent from the pull request? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012e]
- [x] CHK019 Is it stated whether a log row may name a commit sha that was never pushed, given that the reply template and the stop report both cite that sha to a reviewer? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012e]
- [x] CHK020 Is the ordering of commit, push, and log write fixed for the failure case as firmly as it is fixed for the success case? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012e]
- [x] CHK021 Is the accepted-window reasoning extended to the push failure, or does it cover only the bookkeeping-commit window it names? [Resolved, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [x] CHK022 Are requirements defined for a bookkeeping commit that itself fails to push, given that replies are gated on bookkeeping commits having landed? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012e]
- [x] CHK023 Is a retry or no-retry stance stated for transient remote failures, rather than left to the implementation? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012e]
- [x] CHK024 Are the requirements explicit that no failure path may leave a partially written artifact, as distinct from an unpushed but complete one? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]

## Reply Failure Across the Two Surfaces

- [x] CHK025 Are requirements defined for a reply that posts on one surface and fails on the other within the same run? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015b]
- [x] CHK026 Is the interaction between a failed reply and the skip key specified, given that the log row already exists when replies are posted and the skip key reads the log alone? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015b]
- [x] CHK027 Can the exactly-one-reply-per-handled-comment criterion be satisfied when a reply write fails after its row landed, or does the failure make it unreachable? [Resolved, Spec §SC-002]
- [x] CHK028 Is a reconciliation rule specified that lets a later run tell an unreplied handled comment from a replied one, using machinery the requirements already define? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015b]
- [x] CHK029 Is the newer conversation-surface write held to the same failure-handling requirements as the review-thread write, given it has no prior art to inherit behavior from? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015b]
- [x] CHK030 Is it specified whether a reply failure stops the run or is reported and passed over, and is that choice consistent with the amended and non-amended paths? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015b]
- [x] CHK031 Is a reply failure required to appear in the run report the way an exclusion is, so a lost reply is visible rather than silent? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015b]

## Consensus Outcomes That Are Not an Answer

- [x] CHK032 Is the behavior for a consensus round reaching no agreement specified, rather than named as an edge case with no stated outcome? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [x] CHK033 Is the human-review outcome required to surface in both the stop report and the log, rather than being applied or dropped? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [x] CHK034 Is it specified which class a comment takes when consensus returns no usable answer, given that the class set is closed at four and human review is not one of them? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [x] CHK035 Are requirements defined for a second consensus round that escapes and still cannot resolve? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [x] CHK036 Are requirements defined for an analyst that fails or does not return mid-round, given the shipped protocol retries once and then flags the item? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [x] CHK037 Is it stated whether a human-review item blocks the whole run or only its own comment, consistent with the shipped protocol's do-not-block-the-batch rule? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [x] CHK038 Is the deferred wording constraint reconciled with a human-review outcome, given that deferred must not imply future action while human review requires it? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [x] CHK039 Is a comment left unresolved by consensus required to produce a log row, so a later run does not silently reprocess it? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]

## Stop-Condition Composition

- [x] CHK040 Is the set of conditions that stop the run enumerated in one place, rather than accumulating one requirement at a time? [Resolved, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK041 Does the enumeration of existing stop conditions stay accurate after the security domain added a write-point stop and an input-validation error? [Resolved, Spec §FR-012d]
- [x] CHK042 Is the input-validation failure specified as a stop with a report and a resume path, rather than as a bare error return? [Resolved, Spec §FR-006b]
- [x] CHK043 Is one report contract stated for all stop conditions — the condition, what already landed, and the resume path — rather than each stop defining its own shape? [Resolved, Spec §FR-020]
- [x] CHK044 Do the counting phrases used across the requirements and success criteria stay true as stop conditions are added? [Resolved, Spec §SC-011]

## The Proceed-versus-Stop Boundary

- [x] CHK045 Is the boundary between nothing-to-act-on and could-not-read stated as a general principle, rather than only at the one status pair where it first appeared? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]
- [ ] CHK046 Is a zero-comment readable pull request distinguishable in the requirements from a pull request whose comments could not be read? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK047 Is the run report required on every path, including the paths that proceed, so a swept-nothing run is reported rather than silent? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018a]
- [x] CHK048 Is the requirement that a failed observation never counts as a clean state stated for the read paths as well as the corroboration gate? [Resolved, Spec §FR-004c]

## Second Pass (loop 2) — the Remediation's Own Surface

Loop 1 added FR-004c, FR-011a, FR-012e, FR-015b, and FR-020. These items test
the new requirements the way loop 1 tested the old ones, because a fix that
introduces its own ambiguity has moved the gap rather than closed it. Two of
these were live gaps when written and are marked with the requirement text that
now answers them.

- [x] CHK049 Is the reply-reconciliation rule scoped to comments present in the current observation, so a thread a human resolved between runs does not read as a missing reply and draw a duplicate? [Resolved, Spec §FR-015b]
- [x] CHK050 Is the point at which a human-review outcome stops the run stated, so it is clear whether sibling items that resolved still get their replies? [Resolved, Spec §FR-011a]
- [ ] CHK051 Does the stop-condition enumeration list every condition the document defines, with no stop reachable that the list omits? [Consistency, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK052 Is the interaction between the marker's new comment id and the anchored self-reply match specified, so extending the marker cannot break the FR-006 test? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015b]
- [ ] CHK053 Is the term "handled" defined once and used consistently, now that a comment can be observed, trusted, and still take no class? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK054 Is the choice to record a human-review outcome in the Consensus Resolution Log rather than the Feedback Sweep Log justified against the skip key it would otherwise set? [Traceability, Spec §FR-011a]
- [ ] CHK055 Are the added requirements' effects on the reviewability budget recorded rather than absorbed, given the estimate now crosses a block threshold? [Measurability, Plan §Failure Paths]
- [x] CHK056 Do the fixture requirements cover the new failure paths, rather than the requirements growing while the pinned corpus stays where loop 1 left it? [Resolved, Spec §FR-008a]
